bucket.description: An object store addressed by the S3 API. The vendor is not part of the configuration: an endpoint, a region and a path-style flag are enough to reach a cloud service, an in-cluster store or a test double, and a service that hard-codes one of them cannot be tested without it.

ca.description: Path to a certificate authority bundle the platform mounts, for a store whose endpoint is not signed by a public root. A store inside somebody's own network is the ordinary case, not the exotic one. Unset means the system trust store.

credentialsSecret.description: The NAMES of the secrets holding static credentials, never the values, resolved through `secrets`. Unset means the SDK's ambient credentials, which is what a workload identity provides.

endpoint.description: Override the API endpoint. Unset means the SDK's own resolution for the region.

name.description: The bucket. It exists already: a service does not create its own store.

pathStyle.description: Address the bucket as a path rather than as a host. Required by most non-cloud implementations.

region.description: The region the bucket is in.

postgres.description: A PostgreSQL connection. The URL carries no password: a password in it is refused, and `passwordSecret` names the secret that holds it.

maxConnections.description: Pool size for this instance. Sized against the server's limit divided by the number of instances, not guessed.

passwordSecret.description: The NAME of the secret holding the password, resolved through `secrets`. Unset means the connection needs none.

allOf.description: No password in the user information: postgres://user:password@host is refused, postgres://user@host is not.
No password as a query parameter: password= and sslpassword= are refused. passfile= is allowed, because it names a file rather than carrying a secret.
No percent-encoded parameter name: a driver decodes the name before it reads it, so %70assword= is password= by another spelling.

url.description: A connection URL without credentials, for example postgres://user@host:5432/dbname?sslmode=require. A password in the user information or in a password or sslpassword parameter is refused: the file is rendered into objects people read, and the password belongs to `passwordSecret`.

secrets.description: Where a field named `...Secret` finds the secret it names. One source for the whole file: `env` (the name is an environment variable), `file` (the name is a path under `root`, one file per secret: a mounted Kubernetes Secret) or `ssm` (the name is a SecureString under `root` in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, read with the process's own identity). On AWS Lambda use `ssm`: the function's environment is never a place for a secret. Unset is `env`.

root.description: The directory (`file`) or the parameter path (`ssm`, starting with `/`) every secret's name is under. Required with `file` and `ssm`, refused with `env`. A name is relative to it and cannot leave it.

description: The configuration of audit-observe, the indexer: it follows the archive by cursor and writes the index the query service reads (ADR 0020). Secrets are never in this file: a field named ...Secret holds the NAME of a secret, which the `secrets` block says how to find (an environment variable, a file or an SSM parameter). Telemetry is the OTEL_* environment, not configuration.

apiVersion.description: The version of this document's shape, `audit.truvity.github.io/audit-observe/v2`. Absent means version 1, which is deprecated and read for one minor (`truvity.github.io/audit-observe/v1`); another value is refused, so that a later shape arrives by a version and not by a file that quietly means something else.

archive.description: The archive to follow. Observe only reads it: it lists, and gets the objects and the catalogues beside them.

prefix.description: The prefix within the bucket. Required in a bucket shared with other installations: it is what keeps two of them apart.

batch.description: How many rows are written in one transaction. A transaction ends at an object's end, so an object is never split.

database.description: The index, as the role `audit migrate --observe` granted: read and write on the index and its cursors, and nothing of the deduplication table. Not the owner, and not the writer's or the query service's.

interval.description: How often a pass runs when nothing woke it. A lost wake-up costs at most this.

profiles.description: The profiles to follow. Unset follows every profile the archive has, found by listing.

settle.description: How far behind now the cursor stays. An object's key is fixed when its put starts and it is visible when the put ends, so a later key can be visible before an earlier one; this must be longer than a writer's put can take and than the clocks of the writers and of this process can disagree. It is the least time between a record's acknowledgement and its appearance in search.

wake.description: Where bucket notifications arrive, to make a pass run now instead of at the next interval. Optional, and only ever a shortcut: nothing a pass does depends on a notification, so a lost or repeated one costs latency and nothing else.

nats.description: A NATS subject carrying bucket notifications. Core NATS: the messages are not read, and one missed is the poll's to make up.

sqs.description: An SQS queue of bucket notifications that is observe's own: each message is taken to wake a pass and deleted. Credentials are never in the file: the process uses the SDK's ambient ones, which on Kubernetes is the pod's workload identity (EKS Pod Identity or IRSA) bound through the service account.

fifo.description: The queue is FIFO. It must agree with the URL, which ends in `.fifo` for one. A FIFO queue absorbs a repeated record itself, inside its five-minute window; a standard queue relies on the writer's deduplication.

region.description: The queue's region. Unset is the SDK's: AWS_REGION, which EKS Pod Identity and IRSA set.
